facts.text: The pilotbird is a large, plump bird about 18 centimetres long that weighs around 27 grams.
facts.quote: The pilotbird is a large, plump species of acanthizid, measuring around 18 centimetres (7.1 in) in length and weighing 27 grams (0.95 oz).

facts.text: It has reddish-brown underparts with scalloping on the chest, and chocolate-brown upperparts.
facts.quote: The plumage of the underparts is reddish-brown with scalloping on the chest and the centre of the belly speckled dull white. The upperparts are chocolate-brown.

facts.text: Its broad, semi-erect tail is flicked up and down while it feeds.
facts.quote: Its tail is broad and semi-erect, and flicked up and down when feeding.

facts.text: The pilotbird is named for its supposed habit of following lyrebirds to snatch prey they flush.
facts.quote: Its name comes from its supposed habit of following lyrebirds, taking prey that they flush, and also from its call guiding bushmen seeking for lyrebirds.

facts.text: When disturbed on the ground, it runs swiftly away on strong legs.
facts.quote: The pilotbird is highly terrestrial, feeding on or near the ground and when disturbed it runs swiftly on strong legs.

facts.text: The male sings a far-carrying wit-wit-weet-WHEER, which the female may answer with a softer wit-a-wit-ee.
facts.quote: The male makes a far-carrying call of wit-wit-weet-WHEER to which the female may respond with a softer wit-a-wit-ee.

facts.text: From August to December it builds an untidy, globular nest with a side entrance, hidden in debris on the forest floor.
facts.quote: The breeding season for the pilotbird is from August to December. The globular nest is built with a side-entrance and hidden amongst the accumulated debris on the forest floor. It is an untidy construction of bark, ferns, dead leaves and rootlets.

facts.text: The female incubates a clutch of usually two grey-green to purple-brown eggs for 20 to 22 days.
facts.quote: A clutch of usually two eggs, each measuring 27 by 20 mm (1.06 by 0.79 in) and varying in colour from grey-green to purple-brown, is incubated by the female for 20–22 days.

facts.text: The 2019/2020 bushfires burnt 47% of its distribution, prompting a Vulnerable listing under the EPBC Act in 2022.
facts.quote: The pilotbird was listed as Vulnerable under the EPBC Act in 2022, in response to the 2019/2020 Australian Bushfires, which burnt 47% of its distribution, and contributed to an estimated 30-50% decline in the population.
